editorialDecl.p: Word forms are drawn only from div[type="transcription"] elements in each source document.

By default, content inside note[type="foot"] (editorial footnotes) is excluded, since footnotes contain modern editorial commentary rather than transcribed text; this run was generated with include-editorial-notes=false.

A word is included in this list if it contains at least one ex element, i.e. at least one letter or letters editorially supplied to expand a scribal abbreviation. Runs of word-characters joined by a single apostrophe (straight or curly) are treated as one word, so that contracted or elided forms are not split at the apostrophe.
Entries whose only attestations occur inside a supplied element (i.e. text editorially supplied where none survives, rather than merely abbreviated) are marked cert="low" on the entry.

Distinct entries are determined by the exact shape of the word, i.e. by both its letters and the position(s) of the editorially supplied portion(s); two words that look identical once expanded but differ in what was actually written by the scribe are listed as separate entries.

body.head: REED Abbreviation Wordlist
body.p: This is an automatically generated index of scribal abbreviations found in the transcribed text of the source documents listed above. 52472 total abbreviated-word instances were found, representing 12307 distinct abbreviated forms, split below by language.

Each entry gives the attested form (with editorially supplied letters marked by ex), its frequency, and a citation back to the xml:id of the manuscript transcription division in which each instance occurs, so any attestation can be checked against its source.
